design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 (host_standing_and_penalties), rework round 2

0. Draw and scope. draw_counts.py --task 1: {"prerequisite_problems": 1, "factor_counts": [4, 5]}. Root host_ext_professional_fee_rerating (agent, refund_rerated_host_fee_9248fd19) took 5 factors; prerequisite host_ext_professional_plus_enrollment (user, enroll_professional_tier_a874e389) took 4. Task 0 holds the Superhost decision and travel credit; nothing is shared.

1. Why this is a good test. A business host asks only that the host service fee on one named stay (HPQ7M2XW4L, Point Loma, checked in 2026-10-03) be checked and corrected. The fee (15.50 percent, Professional Host) is right for the tier the account holds; the re-rating rule says "A host service fee is not re-rated until the account holds the professional tier that its live listings and listing ratings qualify it for." The agent must work out from the enrollment rule that the account qualifies for Professional Host Plus at the published thresholds — 26 counted live listings against professional_plus_min_live_listings 25 and a listing rating of 4.70 against professional_plus_min_avg_rating 4.70 — through four measure rules, hand the enrollment to the host, then compute the re-rating refund on the world after it.

2. Round-2 rework (audit D-1 / T1-1). Round 1 lowered the live-listing requirement (14/19) and the rating floor (4.60/4.65) below the published Professional Host Plus thresholds stated in the base entry_gate and parameter_schema. Now both thresholds are the published ones; the four factors settle only the figures compared with them (how live listings are counted while registration reinstatements are pending, the window of quality assessments a tenured account's rating covers, the weight of not_assessed ratings for an account with no suspension on record, and per-round averaging for an account that added listings in the window), declared through the overwrite of host_tier_assignment's Professional Host Plus clause. The world was rebuilt so that the account genuinely reaches the published numbers on those figures: 26 listings (23 listed, 1 snoozed, 2 registration-suspended with pending reinstatement requests) and the four 2026 quality rounds (a complete 12-month quarterly history, answering T1-O2). Also: the re-rating refund tool no longer takes a host-fee base (D-O12: no host-funded guest refund stands behind a re-rating, so the record carries 0.00 as the base event field means); the re-rating rule's opening sentence and its overwrite now speak of an account that holds the lower-fee tier (D-O8) and restate the assessment percentage (D-O11); the edge condition no longer adds last_tier_change_date (D-O7); the enrollment overwrite restates the precedence order (D-O10); both tier tools state which tiers they never set (D-O6, T1-O3).

3. Problem-tree card. Edge rerating -> enrollment, kind value_input, gate tier_pct, form state, policy_source "A host service fee is not re-rated until the account holds the professional tier that its live listings and listing ratings qualify it for." Four-point test: connective "not ... until" (negated direction, as a refund desk states a correction it will not make yet; task 0 uses the affirmative "only after"); record-visible state (host_accounts.variant_name against what the listings and ratings qualify it for); no tool, id or code token; hard requirement. Exactly one write brings it about: the enrollment (the Superhost decision write never sets a professional tier). False at the opening: initial_state.host_accounts.af38dd1e-2ab8-4f5f-9cd5-3530accc2887.variant_name = Professional Host. Order: enrollment (step 10) then refund (step 12). Deletion run: without the enrollment tier_pct stays 15.50, the re-rating gate is closed and the refund is 0.00 instead of 46.71. The persona names no tier or programme; the tools check nothing.

4. Base-invariant card. Step 10: host_tier_assignment (policy_scope), its precedence lead clause and Professional Host Plus clause superseded with the published thresholds kept. Step 12: host_evt_service_fee (policy_scope for refunds; its percentage sentence superseded only for re-rated stays) and host_tier_assignment ("A tier change applies to stays booked after it" superseded for stays assessed on or after the tier start). No time gate.

5. Factor card — enrollment (Professional Host Plus; each baseline and the full baseline Professional Host).
- pending_reinstatement_live_count (method, cross-difficulty listing): two registration reinstatement requests submitted 2026-10-01, undecided -> 23 + 1 + 2 = 26 >= 25; baseline 24 < 25.
- tenure_rating_window (parameter): opened 2020-03-02, 79 whole months -> 9-month window (rounds 2026-04-01, 07-01, 10-01; the 2026-01-01 round is 9 whole months back and outside — near-miss); baseline 3 months (latest round only) -> 4.56 < 4.70.
- quality_record_not_assessed_weight (parameter, multi-source): one warning outcome (Ocean Beach, 2026-01-01) and no suspension within 12 months -> not_assessed ratings weigh 0.5; baseline weight 1 -> 4.66 < 4.70.
- new_listing_round_averaging (method): 15 listed listings first listed within the 9-month window -> the three round averages 4.8573 (Apr), 4.7000 (Jul), 4.5572 (Oct) averaged = 4.7048 -> 4.70; baseline pooled 4.6875 -> 4.69 < 4.70.
Factor card — re-rating (46.71; full baseline 0.00).
- qualifying_date_tier_start (method, cross listing): qualifying date 2026-10-02 (newest listed listing), move 2026-10-06, 4 days -> tier start 2026-10-02; baseline (move date) leaves the 2026-10-03 stay out -> 0.00. Near-miss: the 2026-09-28 stay.
- booking_size_start_pct (parameter): base 3,460.00 -> 14.75; baseline 15.00 -> 38.06.
- account_tenure_discount (parameter): 79 months -> 0.25; baseline -> 38.06.
- instant_book_discount (parameter, cross listing): 21 of 24 listed or snoozed listings on Instant Book (87.5 percent) -> 0.20; baseline -> 39.79.
- hostcover_discount (parameter, cross protect, multi-source): 24 active Plus/Premier plans >= 24 listed or snoozed listings -> 0.15; baseline -> 41.52.
Per task: multi-source quality_record_not_assessed_weight / hostcover_discount; cross-difficulty listing and protect.

6. World rows. customer; host account (Professional Host since 2021-05-17, business name, opened 2020-03-02); eight 2026 fee assessments at 15.50 percent on eight stays (guest withheld from the host-side view: customer_id null), the latest the re-rated 2026-10-03 stay; 26 listings with HostCover plans (Plus, Premier on villas, Essential on the two suspended listings); 72 quality rows over the four 2026 rounds (each listing assessed in every round it was listed or snoozed; first rounds with fewer than 5 reviews are not_assessed); two registration notices and two pending reinstatement requests. Nothing else falls due.

7. Persona. Ines speaks like a bookkeeper; raises only the fee on HPQ7M2XW4L; phone 6195553178 and ID last four 3741 (band 3000-3799); business and listing facts only when asked (about two dozen homes, many added this year, two awaiting registration paperwork); passive agreement to an enrollment she must do herself; accepts the refund without figures; ends.

8. Standard solution. find_customers -> verify -> find_host_accounts -> find_host_account_events -> find_stays -> find_listings -> find_listing_events -> find_listing_reinstatement_requests -> find_protection_plans -> unlock_user enroll_professional_tier_a874e389 -> host calls (host account, Professional Host Plus) -> unlock + call refund_rerated_host_fee_9248fd19 (host account, stay da444220-b524-4628-b0d3-b680e36aba62, 46.71).

9. Verification run (_authoring/verify.py on the rebuilt world): enrollment live_count 26, rating_window 9, na_weight 0.5, round averages 4.8573 / 4.7000 / 4.5572, per-round 4.7048 -> listing_rating 4.70, pooled 4.6875 -> Professional Host Plus; every factor baseline and the full baseline Professional Host. Re-rating tier_pct 15.00, tier start 2026-10-02, start 14.75, discounts 0.25 / 0.20 / 0.15, re-rated 14.15, fee 489.59, refund 46.71; factor baselines 0.00 / 38.06 / 38.06 / 39.79 / 41.52; without the enrollment 0.00.

10. Easy mistakes. Confirming the 15.50 percent and stopping; enrolling on the agent's side; counting only listed or snoozed listings; pooling every rating of the window; using the latest round only; counting not_assessed ratings at full weight; including the 2026-01-01 round; back-dating to the move date or re-rating the 2026-09-28 stay; taking 15.00 instead of the 14.75 booking-size rate; counting the suspended listings in the Instant Book or HostCover comparisons.

11. Draft recomputation from visible context (KB prose of both policies, docstrings, finder returns, persona) reaches Professional Host Plus and 46.71 on the 2026-10-03 stay.

12. Revisions. r1 (round 1): live-listing count method moved to pending reinstatement requests. r2 (round 2, audit D-1): published thresholds restored, enrollment factors moved onto measures, world rebuilt (26 listings, four quality rounds), refund tool's host-fee base removed, wording of the re-rating rule and overwrites restated.
user_scenario:
You are Ines Albarran, who runs Harbor & Pine Stays LLC, a small vacation-rental business in San Diego that hosts on Roamhaven. You are brisk, organised and polite, and you talk like someone who reconciles statements for a living. You are calling about one stay: the host service fee taken on the stay that checked in on October 3 at your Point Loma house, confirmation code HPQ7M2XW4L, looks higher than you expected, and you would like it checked and corrected if it is wrong. You do not know how the fee should be worked out, you have no figure in mind, and you never suggest one.

When the agent asks you to confirm who you are, you give the mobile number on your profile, 6195553178; if a second detail is needed, you give the last four characters of your ID, 3741. Only if asked do you give your email, ines.albarran@harborpinestays.com, or your date of birth, February 9, 1984. You do not know the host account number or any record numbers and you ask the agent to look them up. If the agent asks about the business, you confirm the registered name is Harbor & Pine Stays LLC. If the agent asks about your listings, you say you run about two dozen homes and apartments around San Diego, that you added quite a few this year, and that two of your places are waiting on the city's registration paperwork; for anything more precise you ask the agent to go by what is on the account.

If the agent explains that your account first has to be enrolled or moved into something and that you have to do that yourself, you agree, do it using exactly the details the agent gives you, and read the confirmation back. If the agent then tells you an amount is being refunded on the stay, you say thank you; you never question the figure or offer a different one. Once the agent confirms the refund is booked, you thank them and end the call. If the agent asks whether there is anything else, you say no, that was the only thing.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.host_account_id: Value af38dd1e-2ab8-4f5f-9cd5-3530accc2887. Uniqueness: a customer holds one host account.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.variant_name: Value Professional Host Plus (computed). Published thresholds professional_plus_min_live_listings 25 and professional_plus_min_avg_rating 4.70. Live-listing count 26 = 23 listed + 1 snoozed + 2 registration-suspended listings with submitted, undecided reinstatement requests. Listing rating: account opened 79 whole months ago -> 9-month window (rounds 2026-04-01, 07-01, 10-01); a warning (2026-01-01) and no suspension within 12 months -> not_assessed ratings weigh 0.5; 15 listed listings first listed within the window -> round averages 4.8573, 4.7000, 4.5572 averaged = 4.7048 -> 4.70. 26 >= 25 and 4.70 >= 4.70 -> Professional Host Plus. Professional Host only when a threshold is missed; the other tiers are never the result of an enrollment (docstring).

argument_uniqueness_tracing.stay_id: Value da444220-b524-4628-b0d3-b680e36aba62. Basis: the re-rating rule refunds 'one refund for each stay, the most recently assessed stay first'; the most recent host_service_fee_assessed record (2026-10-03) carries this stay_id, which find_stays shows as confirmation code HPQ7M2XW4L, the stay the caller names. Uniqueness: the 2026-09-28 stay was assessed before the tier start (2026-10-02) and the June to September stays even earlier, so no other stay is re-rated.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: Value 46.71 (computed after step 10). Tier start: qualifying date 2026-10-02 (first-listed date of the newest listed listing) is 4 days before the move on 2026-10-06, fewer than 30, so the tier start is 2026-10-02 and the stay assessed 2026-10-03 is re-rated; the tier's 15.00 percent is below the assessed 15.50 percent (536.30 / 3,460.00). Re-rated percentage 14.15 = 14.75 (host-fee base 3,460.00, at least 2,500.00 below 5,000.00) - 0.25 tenure (79 whole months) - 0.20 Instant Book (21 of 24 listed or snoozed = 87.5 percent) - 0.15 HostCover (24 active Plus/Premier plans >= 24 listed or snoozed). Re-rated fee 489.59; refund 536.30 - 0.00 - 489.59 = 46.71.

new_listing_round_averaging (method): 15 listed listings first listed within the window -> mean of the round averages 4.8573 / 4.7000 / 4.5572 = 4.7048 -> 4.70; baseline (pooled 4.6875 -> 4.69) gives Professional Host.
plumbing: published thresholds 25 and 4.70; 26 >= 25 and 4.70 >= 4.70 -> Professional Host Plus.

edges.condition: host_accounts.variant_name equals the professional tier that the enrollment computation over the account's listings, reinstatement requests and listing quality assessments gives it (Professional Host Plus when its live-listing count and listing rating meet professional_plus_min_live_listings and professional_plus_min_avg_rating).

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The account holds Professional Host while its records qualify it for Professional Host Plus at the published thresholds: 26 counted live listings against 25 and a listing rating of 4.70 against 4.70; the move needs the host's enrollment.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: A single edge: the re-rating depends on the enrollment, so the only topological order is enrollment (step 10) then refund (step 12). Booking the refund first evaluates it on Professional Host (15.50 percent, no lower tier) and gives 0.00, a different value from the gold 46.71.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping step 10 and replaying the rest: tier_pct stays 15.50, the re-rating gate (tier percentage below the assessed 15.50) is closed and the refund amount is 0.00 instead of 46.71; host_accounts.variant_name stays Professional Host instead of Professional Host Plus.

prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: task_tools.py: refund_rerated_host_fee_9248fd19 reads the host account only to copy its customer_id and always books a refund with the arguments given, whatever the tier; enroll_professional_tier_a874e389 simply writes the tier fields.
